Aloha! This is my Quarto document for my **Week 13** homework. 

Goals for this homework:

- You have a set of 4 .csv files in data/homework. Each file is a time series of temperature and light data collected in tide pools in Oregon by Jenn Fields.
- Bring in all 4 files and calculate the mean and standard deviation of both temperature (Temp.C) and light (Intensity.lux) for each tide pool.
- Use both a for loop and map() functions in your script (basically, do it twice).

## Load Libraries 
```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(praise)
```

# Method 1: For loop 

## Load Data 
```{r}
# Point to the folder on the computer with all the tide pool data 

TidePath <- here("Week_13", "Data", "homework")

# List all files in that path matching a pattern (here, anything with .csv)
files <- dir(path = TidePath, pattern = ".csv")

files
```
Perfect! Let's move forward 

## Pre-allocate space for the loop
```{r}
tidepool_data <- tibble(filename = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    mean_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    sd_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    mean_light = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    sd_light = rep(NA, length(files)))

tidepool_data
```

Here, I'm calculating the mean & standard deviation of both temperature (Temp.C) and light (Intensity.lux) for each tide pool and saving it 

## Test: Reading in the first file
```{r}
raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(TidePath, "/", files[1]))
head(raw_data)

mean_temp <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_temp

sd_temp <- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_temp

mean_light <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_light

sd_light <- sd(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_light

praise()
```

## Creating the for loop
```{r}
for (i in seq_along(files)) {
  
  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(TidePath, "/", files[i]))
  
  tidepool_data$filename[i] <- files[i]
  tidepool_data$mean_temp[i] <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  tidepool_data$sd_temp[i] <- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  tidepool_data$mean_light[i] <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
  tidepool_data$sd_light[i] <- sd(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
}

tidepool_data

praise() # Slayed 
```

# Method 2: purrr

## Load Data 

```{r}
TidePoolPath_purrr <- here("Week_13", "Data", "homework")

files_purrr <- dir(path = TidePoolPath_purrr, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)

files_purrr
```
Although I already loaded the data, here I am using purrr instead of a for loop.  

## Calculate Mean & Standard Deviation 
```{r}
data <- files_purrr |>
  set_names() |>
  map(read_csv) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "filename") |>
  group_by(filename) |>
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_temp = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_light = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_light = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE))
data
```
